primitives.name: Instinct Transitoriness Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: This leads us to the law of transitoriness, which is this : Many instincts ripen at a certain age and then fade away.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: τ: age [dimensionless, normalized lifespan]; K(τ): instinct intensity [dimensionless, 0-1]; τ₀, τ₁: critical window bounds [dimensionless]; supp(K) = [τ₀, τ₁]
primitives.assumptions: Instinct intensity is a compactly supported function of age; ripening and fading are deterministic; window bounds are species-specific constants.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-transient instincts (feeding, self-preservation) where supp(K) ≈ [0,1]; recurrent instincts (pairing, rearing) where K(τ) has multiple disjoint supports.

layer2.mapping: K(τ) ≡ time-gated attention mask in transformer; τ₀,τ₁ ≡ positional encoding cutoff; habit formation ≡ gradient accumulation during critical steps.
layer2.telemetry: Critical window miss rate; instinct intensity decay constant; recurrence period for multi-support instincts.

primitives.name: Critical Window Habit Formation Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: This leads us to the law of transitoriness, which is this : Many instincts ripen at a certain age and then fade away.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: H: habit strength [dimensionless, 0-1]; O(τ): object encounter indicator [0/1]; K(τ): transitoriness kernel [0-1]; H = ∫ K(τ) O(τ) dτ / ∫ K(τ) dτ
primitives.assumptions: Habit formation is linear in instinct intensity and object presence; habit persists indefinitely post-window; no interference from competing instincts.
primitives.breakdown_regime: O(τ) ≡ 0 ∀τ∈supp(K) → H=0 (permanent nullification); overlapping critical windows with conflicting objects → interference; habit decay if not reinforced.

layer2.mapping: H ≡ integrated gradient during critical steps; O(τ) ≡ data presence mask; persistent habit ≡ frozen weights after critical period; GSE: state transition S_naive → S_habit via Φ.
layer2.telemetry: Habit acquisition rate vs. window exposure duration; asymptotic habit strength; transfer latency to post-window performance.

primitives.name: Critical Window Closure & Response Nullification
primitives.verbatim_quote: Spalding kept some chickens shut up till they were comparatively old, and, speaking of these, he says : <small<span class="docvortex-page-footnote" data-block-type="page_footnote" style="color:6b7280""A chicken that has not heard the call of the mother till until eight or ten days old then hears it as if it heard it not.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: τ_c: critical closure age [dimensionless]; R(τ): response function [0/1]; R(τ) = 𝟙_{τ ≤ τ_c} ⋅ O(τ); τ_c ≈ 0.02-0.03 (8-10 days / lifespan)
primitives.assumptions: Sharp closure at τ_c; no plasticity post-closure; object recognition requires instinct-mediated attention.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Partial closure (gradual decay); cross-modal compensation (visual following despite auditory closure); imprinting reversal via extreme reinforcement.

layer2.mapping: τ_c ≡ hard attention cutoff; R(τ) ≡ gating function; 'hears as if not' ≡ zero gradient flow; GSE: absorbing state S_deaf with no transition to S_follow.
layer2.telemetry: Closure age distribution; post-closure response latency; compensation modality emergence rate.

primitives.name: Recurrent Instinct Kernel with Phase Separation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Some instincts are far less transient than others—those connected with feeding and 'self-preservation'may hardly be transient at all, and some, after fading out for a time, recur as strong as ever, e.g., the instincts of pairing and rearing young.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: K_rec(τ) = Σ_i K_i(τ) where K_i have disjoint supports [τ₀ⁱ, τ₁ⁱ]; τ_sep: inter-support gap [dimensionless]; amplitude A_i ≈ constant across i
primitives.assumptions: Recurrent instincts have identical amplitude across phases; phases are triggered by internal state (hormonal) not external objects; inter-phase gap is species-typical.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Phase fusion (supports merge); amplitude decay across recurrences; phase skipping due to environmental suppression.

layer2.mapping: Multi-support kernel ≡ periodic positional encoding; phase separation ≡ layer-wise critical periods; hormonal trigger ≡ global context vector; GSE: cyclic state transitions S_dormant → S_active.
layer2.telemetry: Inter-recurrence interval; amplitude consistency across phases; phase-specific object sensitivity.

The law of transitoriness defines a compactly supported instinct kernel K(τ) where τ is normalized age. Habit formation H = ∫ K(τ)O(τ)dτ / ∫ K(τ)dτ is a normalized convolution of instinct intensity with object encounter O(τ). Critical window closure at τ_c creates a hard gating: R(τ) = 𝟙_{τ≤τ_c}O(τ), explaining Spalding's chicken that 'hears as if it heard not' post-closure. The absorbing state S_null in GSE emerges when τ_c is missed: no transition S_naive→S_habit occurs, leaving permanent response failure. Recurrent instincts (pairing, rearing) are modeled as multi-support kernel K_rec(τ)=ΣK_i(τ) with disjoint supports, isomorphic to periodic positional encodings or layer-wise critical periods. Non-transient instincts (feeding) have supp(K)≈[0,1]. Dualities: (1) instinct intensity ↔ attention weight; (2) habit formation ↔ gradient accumulation; (3) window closure ↔ gradient masking. Failure modes: interference from overlapping windows, partial closure gradients, cross-modal compensation, phase fusion/skipping in recurrent kernels. The chicken example provides empirical τ_c ≈ 8-10 days, giving dimensionless τ_c ≈ 0.02-0.03 for typical lifespan.

reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Organism as agent with time-limited exploration policy π(τ) = K(τ); environment provides objects O(τ). Agent must acquire habits before τ_c or face permanent capability gap. Recurrent instincts represent scheduled policy updates triggered by internal state (hormones), not external cues. Competing agents (predators, conspecifics) exploit window closure: naive post-closure individuals are vulnerable. Mother hen's enticement is failed policy correction after τ_c.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity: K(τ) and O(τ) must be independently measurable; habit H cannot be inferred from post-window behavior alone. Leakage veto: no habit formation signal from τ>τ_c data; recurrent phases must show disjoint τ-support in telemetry. GSE/GSI separation: GSI calibrates K(τ) prior from population data; GSE executes state transitions using realized O(τ). No back-propagation from GSE outcomes to GSI prior within same τ-cycle.
